Subject: MSA redlines - proposed carve to inspection & evidence cadence

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the performance gains Redwood described. Legal at AllHealth ran our standard MSA + Order Form through procurement and we have a couple of asks around the security exhibit and audit rights before we can sign:

- We cannot accept open-ended on-site inspections or unfettered access.
- Need SOC 2 snapshot (most recent) and a 30-day rolling pen-test notice window; if possible, prefer shared aggregate pen-test findings rather than raw access.
- Proposed evidence cadence: quarterly bundled artifact delivery for SOC 2-related items + a single annual evidence sprint for any ad-hoc requests.

I've attached our annotated MSA redline (AllHealth_MSA_proposed_redline_v1.docx) and a SOC 2 snapshot. Can Redwood propose language that limits inspection to a bounded/staged process and a named evidence cadence? We want to close this this month.

AllHealth

Hi Kacey — thanks for the clear notes and for the redline. Appreciate the timeline pressure.

High-level response (we can formalize as Order Form language / Exhibit A redline):

1) Inspection scope: we can accept a bounded, staged inspection model limited to:
   - SOC 2 Type II evidence and documentation relevant to the services in scope,
   - Penetration testing results limited to executive summaries and identified remediation commitments (not raw exploit details),
   - A named, pre-scheduled annual on-site or remote inspection slot (your choice) plus a 10-business-day notice for follow-on technical sampling.

2) Evidence cadence: propose quarterly artifact package (SOC2 controls mapping, config snapshots for the in-scope services, and a short remediation log) and one annual deeper evidence sprint. Ad-hoc requests outside those windows should route through our security review board and be limited to business-critical asks with a 30-day turnaround target.

3) Pen-test notice: Redwood provides a 30-day notice of pen-test windows that may impact service; we will provide redacted executive summaries within 10 business days of the test closure. Full technical detail is provided only under an NDA + scoped inspection agreement.

Ive drafted suggested exhibit snippets and an Order Form clause in this doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-AllHealth-MSA (see "redwood_proposed_inspection_snippets.docx"). Laura — looping you and Ben for legal/ops redlines. If AllHealth agrees in principle well produce a tracked redline to your document.

Next steps: (1) confirm you accept the staged/bounded model above, (2) confirm quarterly + annual cadence is acceptable, (3) well issue a tracked MSA redline and Order Form appendix.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Tessa / Ben — quick legal take and tracked snippets you can paste into a redline. I kept the language tight to preserve AllHealth's concerns while protecting Redwood operationally.

Suggested exhibit language (short form):
"Inspection and Evidence Requests. Customer may request inspection of Redwood's controls and artifacts limited to the items listed in Exhibit A. Inspections shall be: (a) scheduled in advance; (b) limited to one annual inspection per 12-month period (remote or on-site at Customer's election), and (c) any additional technical sampling shall require mutual agreement and be limited to a 10-business-day sampling window. Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report(s), executive summary of penetration testing results, and a remediation log on a quarterly basis for the in-scope services. Full technical pen-test reports and raw exploit data will be provided only under a mutually-executed non-disclosure agreement and a scoped inspection agreement describing approved personnel and sampling boundaries."

Key points:
- We should keep "one annual inspection" language to avoid recurring unfettered access requests.
- Offer quarterly artifact bundles (controls map, config snapshot, remediation log). That addresses procurement's ask while keeping cadence predictable.
- Pen-test details: provide executive summaries by default; full reports only under NDA + scoped inspection.

Ben — operationally, can you confirm the 10-business-day sampling window and whether we can commit to 30-day turnaround for redacted exec summaries? If so we can attach the snippet as an Exhibit and produce a tracked MSA redline for AllHealth.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
